models_evaluated: AI system for detection of cardiac amyloidosis-associated high-grade cardiac tracer uptake (developed on Austrian data)

links.outcome: AI discrimination (AUC) in independent validation cohorts from different centres
links.effect: Independent validation AUCs: UK 0·997 (0·993-0·999), China 0·925 (0·871-0·971), Italy 1·000 (0·999-1·000); the Chinese cohort was lower.
links.quote: Independent validation yielded AUCs of 0·997 (0·993-0·999) for the UK, 0·925 (0·871-0·971) for the Chinese, and 1·000 (0·999-1·000) for the Italian cohorts.

links.outcome: Robustness of AI performance across demographic factors, tracers, scanners, and centres in an algorithmic audit
links.effect: Audit demonstrated robustness across demographic factors, tracers, scanners, and centres; no details of subgroup numbers in the abstract.
links.quote: The medical algorithmic audit demonstrated the system's robustness across demographic factors, tracers, scanners, and centres.

links.outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with five physicians on the same 200 cases
links.effect: Physicians' mean AUC 0·946 (0·924-0·967) was inferior to AI AUC 0·997 (0·991-1·000), p=0·0040; physicians disagreed in 22 (11%) of 200 cases.
links.quote: In the multicase multireader study, five physicians disagreed in 22 (11%) of 200 cases (Fleiss' kappa 0·89), with a mean AUC of 0·946 (95% CI 0·924-0·967), which was inferior to AI (AUC 0·997 [0·991-1·000], p=0·0040).

unlisted_practices: Using AI prediction of scintigraphy uptake as a prognostic marker for mortality

screen.reason: Multicentre retrospective validation, reader study comparing clinicians with AI, and algorithmic audit of failure modes for cardiac scintigraphy AI.
